prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1460; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact at an intersection involving our insured vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver of the vehicle is named on it. Coverage was in force on the date of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. Two independent witnesses describe the crash in the same sequence the claimant gave.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement agree with the reported accident sequence. The damage to the vehicle is mostly consistent with the described side impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 5: Counsel submitted the medical file showing a wrist fracture. The injury fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type, and no prior injury to the same area appears in the records we have.

Entry 6: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation so far, including the initial call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up through counsel.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. The provider notes show steady improvement, and visit frequency has tapered as the patient recovered.

Entry 8: Reviewed the bills and treatment timeline against the injury. The care pattern is consistent with a standard recovery for this fracture, and no unusual gaps or escalations appear.

Entry 9: File is in order on liability, damage, injury and coverage. Next step is to finalize the injury evaluation with counsel and set a settlement conference.
